card.text: A physical explanation must say when it applies; a definition must survive difficult counterexamples. Both give us ways to challenge a claim against a particular case. The standing of the person making a claim does not answer those challenges.

intelligibility.explanation: The rule contributes a universal-seeming requirement to return debts and the weapon request supplies a harmful counterexample. The result explicitly remains an unfinished definition. I could explain each later operand: prestige rejects praise/custom as justification, and the eclipse explanation supplies applicability conditions.

learning.explanation: Within this partial-context assigned scene, I can state the distinction between exposing a definition as inadequate and supplying a better definition. I can also explain how applicability conditions and counterexamples are different ways of making claims answerable to cases. This is evidence of legibility and recall in a logical player, not a claim about human learning gain.

construction.explanation: The first combination genuinely changed a plausible rule into a definition needing further examination. Its reuse with prestige yielded examining a life instead of accepting social approval, and its reuse with conditional explanation yielded challengeable claims. Neither operand in these three combinations was unexplained after the useful optional reads.

pacing.explanation: Three combinations formed a short coherent arc and three optional reads were sufficient. The initial chapter card stayed above the first earned card, requiring dismissal before I could see the result explanation. Later cards arrived directly once I cleared earlier ones. This only assesses this CLI checkpoint scene, not whole-campaign or human pacing.

continuity.explanation: The local bridge from an inherited eclipse explanation to the ethics scene is intelligible after reading the condition item: each lets a particular case challenge a claim, without pretending physical explanation and moral definition are identical. I did not play the preceding 26 setup actions or the later campaign, so broader narrative continuity is unknown.

choice.explanation: There was one unique starting pair, followed by two unique branches and then one remaining pair. I selected the ethics branch before the general-method branch on thematic grounds, but the available choices chiefly changed order; both goals required their outputs. This does not establish open-ended deduction or consequential choice.

report.experience: Partial-context assigned chapterIndex 3 only, entered at a legally prepared checkpoint after 26 developer setup actions. My own successful actions were 27 through 35. The scene was understandable without reading everything: I read the justice rule, prestige, and inherited conditions. At event 35 the final combination made explicit that a physical explanation must name when it applies and a definition must survive counterexamples; both can be challenged by cases regardless of the claimant standing. No operand contribution remained unclear. This is a source-isolated logical-player account, not evidence of fresh whole-campaign experience or human enjoyment.
report.stoppingReason: Both assigned scene goals were complete at event 35. I stopped at chapterIndex 3 without advancing, with the final earned card visible.
report.nextExperiment: Use a new human or otherwise independent fresh player to ask for an unaided explanation of the two final operands and a novel counterexample after the scene. Measure whether the role distinction transfers, and separately test the card queue with the chapter card still visible.
